proposed_constraints.claim: Section-template trace executor with 4-layer hierarchy produces monotonic improvement in multi-axis token execution prediction (domain + hazard + routing + closure): E4 >= E3 >= E2 > E1. Composite LL improvement 2.4% from section-only to full context.

Paragraph emphasis cloud under leave-one-out E3/E4 contextualization recovers folio-specific distributional geometry not available to section-only or folio-average priors. However, paragraph-level domain refinement does NOT improve per-token prediction (E3 = E2 for domain LL).

Packet-destroying nulls collapse hierarchical trace fidelity (N1 token-shuffle z=14.1, N4 within-domain form-shuffle z=8.8), confirming context contribution is non-trivial and not reducible to domain inventory alone.

E4 trace improvement over E2 comes from line-phase domain adjustment (+0.0076 domain axis) and hazard envelope adjustment (+0.0039 hazard axis). Closure phase gating is counterproductive (WORK_SEMI at 87% dominance makes redistribution harmful). Routing and headless axes are folio-level, not line-level.

narrative: Phase 562 constructed and validated a hierarchical trace executor operating across the 5-layer stack (section -> folio -> paragraph -> line -> token) for Currier B. The executor processes 23096 tokens through 4 progressively enriched context modes. Multi-axis prediction improves monotonically: E4 composite LL = -3.2832 vs E1 = -3.3635 (improvement: 2.4%). The hierarchy is validated as contributing real information at each level. Paragraph cloud structural recovery confirms that hierarchical context produces folio-specific paragraph distributions, not just section-level averages (P2 PASS). Primary contributors to E4 improvement: domain axis (+0.0458, from phase adjustment + routing mask) and hazard axis (+0.0195, from envelope adjustment). E3 paragraph cloud does not improve per-token domain prediction (E3 = E2 for domain LL) -- paragraph-level domain refinement is noisier than the folio average. This is consistent with C1573's finding that folio specificity lives in distributional SHAPE, not in per-token mean position. Token-shuffle null (N1 z=14.1) confirms the hierarchy is non-trivial: destroying local structure collapses trace quality. Within-domain form-shuffle null (N4 z=8.8) confirms that compositional token structure (terminals, modifiers, suffixes) carries information beyond domain inventory alone.
scope_note: Phase 562 validates the executor SUBSTRATE, not the executor itself. The traces show that hierarchical context improves token-level prediction, and that removing layers degrades it. Key limitation: E3 paragraph cloud does not improve per-token LL (domain axis), confirming that paragraph-level distributional specificity operates at the aggregate level (cloud geometry), not at the token level. Closure phase gating (CLOSURE_PHASE_MASK) was disabled because WORK_SEMI dominance (87%) makes any redistribution harmful to LL. This is a property of the closure class distribution, not a failure of the architectural model.

design_notes.E3_domain_equals_E2: Paragraph kNN domain refinement is noisier than folio average. E3 value is in cloud geometry recovery (P2), not per-token LL.
design_notes.closure_mask_disabled: CLOSURE_PHASE_MASK disabled: WORK_SEMI at 87% makes any redistribution harmful. Folio-level closure prior is optimal.
design_notes.source_immune_correction: source_immune covers ALL headed tokens (C1546) plus quench-modified headless (C1450), NOT just k-HEAD. IMMUNE hazard posture restricted to k-HEAD only (C1446/C1476).
